hpi: {{patient_name}} is a neonate/infant presenting with bilious (green) vomiting — a surgical emergency until proven otherwise. Bilious vomiting in a newborn = malrotation with volvulus. Malrotation occurs when the midgut fails to complete its normal 270° counterclockwise rotation during fetal development, resulting in a narrow mesenteric base. This predisposes to volvulus — twisting of the midgut around the superior mesenteric artery → intestinal ischemia and necrosis. Diagnosis: upper GI series (gold standard) showing DJJ (duodenojejunal junction) to the RIGHT of midline and spiral/corkscrew duodenum. Abdominal X-ray may show double bubble sign or gasless abdomen. Treatment: EMERGENCY surgical exploration (Ladd procedure). NPO, NG tube decompression, IV fluids. Time-critical — delay leads to bowel necrosis and short gut syndrome.
